findings: All 33 NPU packets pass. The fresh guest and 120-second sole-indirect display observation still deliver no frames. DWM and Explorer both run in session 1.
DWM creates two devices and produces the same 123-event trace structure as v79, with no draw or Present. IDD prepares its device and commits a display mode but receives no swapchain.

The slow-packet mechanism preserves four complete real Explorer requests. One is dominated by compilation (11.25 s total versus 47 ms draw); others visit 432, 90 and 234 triangle tiles for 49152, 868 and 872 covered samples.
A later 36-vertex shell draw visits 1296 tiles for only 373 covered samples, taking 21.35 s draw time and 33.27 s including compilation.

The final successful NPU request is not recorded as a completed UMD draw before teardown; one Explorer draw rejection follows during cleanup. Both custom devices are removed, topology restored, and ETW stopped successfully.
No physical driver or Tahoma changes are made. This experiment does not establish performance benefit or full desktop rendering.
